section_1.title: The Concept of 'Inverse' Operations
section_1.content: Introduce the idea that many mathematical operations have a 'reverse' partner. This sets the stage for the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus by relating it to familiar concepts like addition/subtraction and multiplication/division.
section_1.example: Imagine a 'Mathematical Time Machine': if adding 5 moves a character 5 steps forward, subtracting 5 brings them back to the start. We will discover if the same exists for Calculus.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Review: The Derivative as a 'Rate'
section_2.content: Briefly revisit the derivative as the instantaneous rate of change or the slope of a tangent line. Use a graphical representation of a curve where a moving point shows the changing slope.
section_2.example: An animation of a car driving up a hill: the speedometer shows the 'Derivative' (velocity) at every specific point on the slope.

section_3.title: Prerequisite Review: The Integral as 'Accumulation'
section_3.content: Define the definite integral as the area under a curve. Visualize this by filling the space under a velocity-time graph with thin rectangles (Riemann sums) that merge into a solid color.
section_3.example: A 'Digital Rain Gauge': as rain falls at varying intensities (the function), the total water collected in the bucket represents the Integral (the area/accumulation).

section_4.title: The Bridge: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
section_4.content: Explain the core relationship: Differentiation and Integration are inverse processes. If you integrate a function and then differentiate the result, you return to the original function.
section_4.example: Display the equation d/dx [ ∫ f(t) dt ] = f(x). Show a 'Function Factory' where a raw material goes through an 'Integrator' machine and then a 'Differentiator' machine, coming out exactly as it started.

section_5.title: Visualizing the Connection: The Area Function
section_5.content: Animate a moving vertical line (x) that 'paints' the area under a curve f(t). Show that the rate at which this area grows at any moment is exactly equal to the height of the function at that point.
section_5.example: A 'Growing Carpet' animation: As a character unrolls a carpet (the area), the speed at which the carpet area increases is determined by the width of the roll (the function's value f(x)).

section_6.title: Real-World Application: The Racing Cheetah
section_6.content: Apply the concept to physics. If we know the velocity (derivative of position), we can find the total distance (integral). Conversely, if we have the distance, we can find the velocity.
section_6.example: A Cheetah sprints. Graph 1 (Velocity): The area under the curve shows the Cheetah moved 100 meters. Graph 2 (Position): The slope of this line at 3 seconds matches the height of Graph 1 at 3 seconds.

section_7.title: Summary and Conclusion
section_7.content: Recap the 'Inverse' relationship. Emphasize that the integral allows us to find the 'net change' by knowing the 'rate of change', and vice versa.
section_7.example: Final split-screen: Left side shows 'Slope Calculation' (Derivative), right side shows 'Area Calculation' (Integral), with a bridge connecting them labeled 'Calculus'.

section_6.content: Apply the concept to physics. If we know the velocity (derivative of position), we can find the total distance (integral). Conversely, if we have the distance, we can find the velocity.
section_6.example: A Cheetah sprints. Graph 1 (Velocity): The area under the curve shows the Cheetah moved 100 meters. Graph 2 (Position): The slope of this line at 3 seconds matches the height of Graph 1 at 3 seconds.

section_7.title: Summary and Conclusion
section_7.content: Recap the 'Inverse' relationship. Emphasize that the integral allows us to find the 'net change' by knowing the 'rate of change', and vice versa.

section_1.title: The Concept of 'Inverse' Operations
lecture_lines: Mathematics often uses operations that reverse each other.
Addition and subtraction are perfect examples of this.
Can we find a reverse partner for calculus?
animations: Show character at point 'Start' on a horizontal line.
Move character forward 5 units with Green (#00FF00) arrow.
Move character back 5 units with Red (#FF0000) arrow.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Review: The Derivative as a 'Rate'
lecture_lines: Derivatives measure the instantaneous rate of change.
We visualize this as the slope of a curve.
It tells us how fast a value is changing.
animations: Draw a white curve (#FFFFFF) with a moving point.
Display a yellow tangent line (#FFFF00) at the moving point.
Show the slope value changing as the point moves.

section_3.title: Prerequisite Review: The Integral as 'Accumulation'
lecture_lines: Integrals represent the accumulation of values over time.
We calculate this as the area under a curve.
This area sums up all the small changes.
animations: Draw a white curve (#FFFFFF) on a black background.
Fill the region below with thin Blue (#0000FF) rectangles.
Merge rectangles into a solid Blue (#0000FF) area block.

section_4.title: The Bridge: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are actually inverse processes.
This link is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
Integrating then differentiating returns the original function.
It connects slopes and areas through a single bridge.
Calculus is a two-way street between these concepts.
animations: Display the integral expression in Blue (#0000FF).
Surround the integral with a Green (#00FF00) derivative operator.
Show the expression simplify into the original function f(x).
Animate a 'Factory' box transforming area back into height.
Highlight the final f(x) in White (#FFFFFF) with a glow.

section_5.title: Visualizing the Connection: The Area Function
lecture_lines: Let's define a function for the accumulating area.
As we move right, the total area grows.
The rate of growth depends on the function's height.
Taller curves add area faster than shorter ones.
The derivative of area is the original function.
animations: Draw white curve f(t) and a sliding vertical line.
Shade area behind the sliding line in Yellow (#FFFF00).
Place a red dot (#FF0000) on curve at sliding line.
Show the area's rate of change equals the height f(x).
Flash the connection between area growth and curve height.

section_6.title: Real-World Application: The Racing Cheetah
lecture_lines: A cheetah's velocity is the derivative of its position.
The area under the velocity curve is distance traveled.
We can calculate distance by integrating the velocity function.
Conversely, differentiate position to find the cheetah's speed.
These two measurements are mathematically linked.
animations: Display a green velocity-time graph (#00FF00) for a cheetah.
Fill the area under velocity graph in Blue (#0000FF).
Draw a white position-time graph (#FFFFFF) in split-screen.
Animate a yellow tangent line (#FFFF00) on position graph.
Show tangent slope value equals the velocity graph height.

section_7.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: The Bridge connects rates of change with accumulation.
Derivatives and integrals are two sides of one coin.
This relationship is the heart of calculus.
animations: Show 'Slope' (#FFFF00) and 'Area' (#0000FF) icons side-by-side.
Draw a gold bridge (#FFD700) connecting both icons.
Pulse 'Fundamental Theorem of Calculus' text in White (#FFFFFF).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Visualizing the Connection: The Area Function"
        lines = [
            "Let's define a function for the accumulating area.",
            "As we move right, the total area grows.",
            "The rate of growth depends on the function's height.",
            "Taller curves add area faster than shorter ones.",
            "The derivative of area is the original function."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_CURVE = WHITE
        COLOR_AREA = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_DOT = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_FORMULA = "#00FFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Let's define a function for the accumulating area.
        # Draw white curve f(t) and a sliding vertical line.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_CURVE)
        
        # Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 6, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY},
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "F6", scale_factor=0.85)
        
        # Curve f(t) = 0.1t^2 + 1
        func = lambda t: 0.1 * t**2 + 1
        curve = axes.plot(func, x_range=[0, 5], color=COLOR_CURVE)
        
        curve_label = MathTex(r"f(t)", color=COLOR_CURVE)
        self.place_at_grid(curve_label, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # ValueTracker for x
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(1)
        
        # Sliding vertical line
        # Use a lambda to keep it updated with x_tracker
        vline = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_vertical_line(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=2
        ))
        
        x_label = always_redraw(lambda: MathTex("x", color=WHITE).next_to(vline, DOWN, buff=0.1))

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), Write(curve_label))
        self.play(Create(vline), Write(x_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # As we move right, the total area grows.
        # Shade area behind the sliding line in Yellow (#FFFF00).
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_AREA)
        
        area = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_area(
            curve,
            x_range=[0, x_tracker.get_value()],
            color=COLOR_AREA,
            opacity=0.4
        ))
        
        area_label = MathTex(r"A(x) = \int_0^x f(t) dt", color=COLOR_AREA)
        self.place_at_grid(area_label, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.add(area)
        self.play(Write(area_label))
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The rate of growth depends on the function's height.
        # Place a red dot (#FF0000) on curve at sliding line.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_DOT)
        
        dot = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color=COLOR_DOT
        ))
        
        height_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 0),
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color=COLOR_DOT,
            stroke_width=4
        ))
        
        height_label = always_redraw(lambda: MathTex(r"f(x)", color=COLOR_DOT).next_to(dot, UP, buff=0.1))

        self.play(Create(dot), Create(height_line), Write(height_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Taller curves add area faster than shorter ones.
        # Show the area's rate of change equals the height f(x).
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_FORMULA)
        
        # Demonstrate growth by moving x again
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=2)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(5), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The derivative of area is the original function.
        # Flash the connection between area growth and curve height.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        
        ftc_formula = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx} A(x) = f(x)", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(ftc_formula, "F3", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(ftc_formula))
        self.play(
            Indicate(ftc_formula, color=COLOR_DOT),
            Indicate(height_line, color=COLOR_DOT),
            Indicate(height_label, color=COLOR_DOT),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Bridge: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus",
            [
                "Differentiation and integration are actually inverse processes.",
                "This link is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.",
                "Integrating then differentiating returns the original function.",
                "It connects slopes and areas through a single bridge.",
                "Calculus is a two-way street between these concepts."
            ]
        )

        # Colors
        BLUE_COLOR = "#0000FF"
        GREEN_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the integral expression in Blue (#0000FF).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE_COLOR)
        integral_expr = MathTex(r"\int_{a}^{x} f(t) \, dt", color=BLUE_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(integral_expr, "B2", "C5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(integral_expr))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Surround the integral with a Green (#00FF00) derivative operator.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN_COLOR)
        
        # Create full expression to replace current one
        derivative_op = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx}", r"\left[", r"\int_{a}^{x} f(t) \, dt", r"\right]", color=GREEN_COLOR)
        derivative_op[2].set_color(BLUE_COLOR) # Keep integral blue
        self.place_in_area(derivative_op, "B2", "C5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Transform(integral_expr, derivative_op))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show the expression simplify into the original function f(x).
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE_COLOR)
        
        # Position it to the right of the derivative expression or replace it
        final_eq = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx} \left[ \int_{a}^{x} f(t) \, dt \right] = f(x)")
        # Apply colors to parts
        final_eq[0][:4].set_color(GREEN_COLOR) # d/dx
        final_eq[0][4].set_color(GREEN_COLOR) # [
        final_eq[0][5:13].set_color(BLUE_COLOR) # integral
        final_eq[0][13].set_color(GREEN_COLOR) # ]
        final_eq[0][14:].set_color(WHITE_COLOR) # = f(x)
        
        self.place_in_area(final_eq, "B1", "C6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Transform(integral_expr, final_eq))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Animate a 'Factory' box transforming area back into height.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a simple factory box
        factory_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=1.5, color=GREY, fill_opacity=0.5)
        factory_label = Text("FTC Factory", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        factory_group = VGroup(factory_box, factory_label)
        self.place_in_area(factory_group, "E2", "F5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Area representation (Input)
        area_rect = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=0.5, color=BLUE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8)
        area_label = Text("Area", font_size=14, color=BLUE_COLOR)
        area_in = VGroup(area_rect, area_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(area_in, "E1")
        
        # Height representation (Output)
        height_line = Line(ORIGIN, UP * 0.8, color=WHITE_COLOR, stroke_width=4)
        height_label = Text("f(x)", font_size=14, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        height_out = VGroup(height_line, height_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(height_out, "E6")

        self.play(Create(factory_group))
        self.play(FadeIn(area_in))
        
        # Move Area into factory, then output f(x)
        self.play(area_in.animate.move_to(factory_group.get_center()))
        self.play(FadeOut(area_in))
        self.play(FadeIn(height_out, shift=RIGHT))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Highlight the final f(x) in White (#FFFFFF) with a glow.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE_COLOR)
        
        # Create a "glow" effect using multiple rectangles
        glows = VGroup(*[
            SurroundingRectangle(integral_expr, color=WHITE, buff=0.1 + i*0.05, stroke_width=2)
            for i in range(3)
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(glows))
        self.play(
            glows.animate.set_stroke(width=10, opacity=0.3),
            run_time=1,
            rate_func=there_and_back
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching storyboard data
        title = "Prerequisite Review: The Derivative as a 'Rate'"
        lines = [
            "Derivatives measure the instantaneous rate of change.",
            "We visualize this as the slope of a curve.",
            "It tells us how fast a value is changing."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Define colors for synchronization
        CURVE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        TANGENT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        SLOPE_COLOR = "#00FFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line 1: Derivatives measure the instantaneous rate of change.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(CURVE_COLOR))
        
        # Area B2 to E5 for axes and curve
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": GREY},
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        # Curve: f(x) = 0.5x^2 + 1
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2 + 1, color=CURVE_COLOR)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line 2: We visualize this as the slope of a curve.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(TANGENT_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Tracker for x-coordinate to drive the point and tangent line
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(-1.2)
        
        # Tangent line updated in place
        tangent = Line(color=TANGENT_COLOR)
        def update_tangent(line):
            x0 = x_tracker.get_value()
            y0 = 0.5 * x0**2 + 1
            slope = x0 # Derivative of 0.5x^2 + 1 is x
            # Extend line segments symmetrically from the point
            p1 = axes.c2p(x0 - 0.9, y0 - 0.9 * slope)
            p2 = axes.c2p(x0 + 0.9, y0 + 0.9 * slope)
            line.set_points_as_corners([p1, p2])
        
        # Initial position
        update_tangent(tangent)
        tangent.add_updater(update_tangent)
        
        # Moving point on curve
        dot = Dot(color=TANGENT_COLOR)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 0.5 * x_tracker.get_value()**2 + 1)))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Create(tangent))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line 3: It tells us how fast a value is changing.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(SLOPE_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Slope value label placed at the top of the visualization area
        slope_label = MathTex(r"\text{Slope} = ", color=SLOPE_COLOR)
        slope_value = DecimalNumber(x_tracker.get_value(), num_decimal_places=2, color=SLOPE_COLOR)
        slope_group = VGroup(slope_label, slope_value).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        # Use place_in_area for centering the multi-element group
        self.place_in_area(slope_group, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Efficiently update decimal number value in place
        slope_value.add_updater(lambda v: v.set_value(x_tracker.get_value()))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(slope_group))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Animate the movement of the point, updating tangent and slope display
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(1.2), run_time=5, rate_func=smooth)
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(-1.2), run_time=3, rate_func=smooth)
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        # Teaching Content
        lecture_lines = [
            "- A cheetah's velocity is the derivative of its position.",
            "- The area under the velocity curve is distance traveled.",
            "- We can calculate distance by integrating the velocity function.",
            "- Conversely, differentiate position to find the cheetah's speed.",
            "- These two measurements are mathematically linked."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: The Racing Cheetah", lecture_lines)

        # Color Palette
        VELOCITY_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        AREA_COLOR = "#0000FF"
        POSITION_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        TANGENT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"

        # Velocity Axes and Graph (Top Half)
        ax_v = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 3, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 20},
            tips=False
        )
        labels_v = ax_v.get_axis_labels(x_label="t", y_label="v(t)")
        v_func = lambda t: 0.5 * t
        v_graph = ax_v.plot(v_func, color=VELOCITY_COLOR)
        v_group = VGroup(ax_v, labels_v, v_graph)
        self.place_in_area(v_group, "A1", "C5", scale_factor=0.7)

        # Position Axes and Graph (Bottom Half)
        ax_s = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 20},
            tips=False
        )
        labels_s = ax_s.get_axis_labels(x_label="t", y_label="s(t)")
        s_func = lambda t: 0.25 * t**2
        s_graph = ax_s.plot(s_func, color=POSITION_COLOR)
        s_group = VGroup(ax_s, labels_s, s_graph)
        self.place_in_area(s_group, "D1", "F5", scale_factor=0.7)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(VELOCITY_COLOR))
        self.play(Create(ax_v), Write(labels_v))
        self.play(Create(v_graph))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(AREA_COLOR))
        area = ax_v.get_area(v_graph, x_range=[0, 4], color=AREA_COLOR, opacity=0.4)

Shade area behind the sliding line in Yellow (#FFFF00).
Place a red dot (#FF0000) on curve at sliding line.

            "Let's define a function for the accumulating area.",
            "As we move right, the total area grows.",
            "The rate of growth depends on the function's height.",
            "Taller curves add area faster than shorter ones.",
            "The derivative of area is the original function."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_CURVE = WHITE
        COLOR_AREA = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_DOT = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_TEXT = "#00FFFF"

        # Axes setup
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 6, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY},
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Curve f(t) = 0.1t^2 + 1
        func = lambda t: 0.1 * t**2 + 1
        curve = axes.plot(func, x_range=[0, 5.5], color=COLOR_CURVE)
        
        # Use Text instead of MathTex (B008)
        curve_label = Text("f(t)", font_size=20, color=COLOR_CURVE)
        self.place_at_grid(curve_label, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # ValueTracker for x
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Let's define a function for the accumulating area.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_CURVE)
        
        # Sliding vertical line
        # Use a lambda for simple objects but avoid heavy ones
        vline = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_vertical_line(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=2
        ))
        
        # Pre-create text to avoid recreation in always_redraw
        x_label = Text("x", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        x_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(vline, DOWN, buff=0.1))

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), Write(curve_label))
        self.play(Create(vline), FadeIn(x_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # As we move right, the total area grows.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_AREA)
        
        area = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_area(
            curve,
            x_range=[0, x_tracker.get_value()],
            color=COLOR_AREA,
            opacity=0.4
        ))
        
        area_label = Text("A(x) = Area from 0 to x", font_size=20, color=COLOR_AREA)
        self.place_at_grid(area_label, "A3", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.add(area)
        self.play(Write(area_label))
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(4.5), run_time=3, rate_func=rate_functions.linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The rate of growth depends on the function's height.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_DOT)
        
        # Use simple shapes and updates
        dot = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color=COLOR_DOT
        ))
        
        height_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 0),
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color=COLOR_DOT,
            stroke_width=4
        ))
        
        height_label = Text("f(x)", font_size=20, color=COLOR_DOT)
        height_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(dot, UP, buff=0.1))

        self.play(Create(dot), Create(height_line), FadeIn(height_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Taller curves add area faster than shorter ones.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_TEXT)
        
        # Demonstrate growth by moving x again
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=2)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(5.0), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The derivative of area is the original function.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # A'(x) = f(x)
        ftc_formula = Text("Rate of Area Growth = f(x)", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(ftc_formula, "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(ftc_formula))
        self.play(
            Indicate(ftc_formula, color=COLOR_DOT),
            Indicate(height_line, color=COLOR_DOT),
            Indicate(height_label, color=COLOR_DOT),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: The Concept of 'Inverse' Operations
section_1.content: Introduce the idea that many mathematical operations have a 'reverse' partner. This sets the stage for the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus by relating it to familiar concepts like addition/subtraction and multiplication/division.
section_1.example: Imagine a 'Mathematical Time Machine': if adding 5 moves a character 5 steps forward, subtracting 5 brings them back to the start. We will discover if the same exists for Calculus.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Review: The Derivative as a 'Rate'
section_2.content: Briefly revisit the derivative as the instantaneous rate of change or the slope of a tangent line. Use a graphical representation of a curve where a moving point shows the changing slope.
section_2.example: An animation of a car driving up a hill: the speedometer shows the 'Derivative' (velocity) at every specific point on the slope.

section_3.title: Prerequisite Review: The Integral as 'Accumulation'
section_3.content: Define the definite integral as the area under a curve. Visualize this by filling the space under a velocity-time graph with thin rectangles (Riemann sums) that merge into a solid color.
section_3.example: A 'Digital Rain Gauge': as rain falls at varying intensities (the function), the total water collected in the bucket represents the Integral (the area/accumulation).

section_4.title: The Bridge: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
section_4.content: Explain the core relationship: Differentiation and Integration are inverse processes. If you integrate a function and then differentiate the result, you return to the original function.
section_4.example: Display the equation d/dx [ ∫ f(t) dt ] = f(x). Show a 'Function Factory' where a raw material goes through an 'Integrator' machine and then a 'Differentiator' machine, coming out exactly as it started.

section_5.title: Visualizing the Connection: The Area Function
section_5.content: Animate a moving vertical line (x) that 'paints' the area under a curve f(t). Show that the rate at which this area grows at any moment is exactly equal to the height of the function at that point.
section_5.example: A 'Growing Carpet' animation: As a character unrolls a carpet (the area), the speed at which the carpet area increases is determined by the width of the roll (the function's value f(x)).

section_6.title: Real-World Application: The Racing Cheetah
section_6.content: Apply the concept to physics. If we know the velocity (derivative of position), we can find the total distance (integral). Conversely, if we have the distance, we can find the velocity.
section_6.example: A Cheetah sprints. Graph 1 (Velocity): The area under the curve shows the Cheetah moved 100 meters. Graph 2 (Position): The slope of this line at 3 seconds matches the height of Graph 1 at 3 seconds.

section_7.title: Summary and Conclusion
section_7.content: Recap the 'Inverse' relationship. Emphasize that the integral allows us to find the 'net change' by knowing the 'rate of change', and vice versa.
section_7.example: Final split-screen: Left side shows 'Slope Calculation' (Derivative), right side shows 'Area Calculation' (Integral), with a bridge connecting them labeled 'Calculus'.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title_text = "The Concept of 'Inverse' Operations"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Mathematics often uses operations that reverse each other.",
            "Addition and subtraction are perfect examples of this.",
            "Can we find a reverse partner for calculus?"
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors for matching
        COLOR_ADD = "#00FF00"  # Green
        COLOR_SUB = "#FF0000"  # Red
        COLOR_CALC = "#00FFFF" # Cyan
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight: Mathematics often uses operations that reverse each other.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Visual for "Reverse" concept: A bidirectional loop
        rev_arrow_1 = Arrow(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color=WHITE).shift(UP*0.2)
        rev_arrow_2 = Arrow(start=RIGHT, end=LEFT, color=WHITE).shift(DOWN*0.2)
        rev_group = VGroup(rev_arrow_1, rev_arrow_2)
        self.place_in_area(rev_group, "B3", "B4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Create(rev_group))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight: Addition and subtraction are perfect examples of this.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_ADD),
            FadeOut(rev_group)
        )
        
        # Create Number Line
        nl = NumberLine(
            x_range=[0, 10, 1],
            length=4.5,
            include_numbers=True,
            font_size=20,
            color=WHITE
        )
        self.place_in_area(nl, "D2", "D6")
        
        # Character (a small triangle representing the 'Mathematical Time Machine' occupant)
        character = Triangle(color=BLUE, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.2)
        # Manually offset relative to the point on the number line using the object's position
        character.move_to(nl.n2p(0) + UP * 0.4)
        
        start_label = Text("Start", font_size=18).next_to(nl.n2p(0), DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(nl), FadeIn(character), Write(start_label))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Addition: Move character +5 units forward
        add_arrow = Arrow(
            start=nl.n2p(0) + UP * 0.8, 
            end=nl.n2p(5) + UP * 0.8, 
            color=COLOR_ADD, 
            buff=0
        )
        add_text = MathTex("+5", color=COLOR_ADD, font_size=30).next_to(add_arrow, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(add_arrow),
            Write(add_text),
            character.animate.move_to(nl.n2p(5) + UP * 0.4),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Subtraction: Move character back -5 units to start
        # Change color of lecture line to highlight the reversal aspect
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_SUB))
        
        sub_arrow = Arrow(
            start=nl.n2p(5) + UP * 1.4, 
            end=nl.n2p(0) + UP * 1.4, 
            color=COLOR_SUB, 
            buff=0
        )
        sub_text = MathTex("-5", color=COLOR_SUB, font_size=30).next_to(sub_arrow, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(sub_arrow),
            Write(sub_text),
            character.animate.move_to(nl.n2p(0) + UP * 0.4),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight: Can we find a reverse partner for calculus?
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_CALC),
            FadeOut(nl), FadeOut(character), FadeOut(start_label),
            FadeOut(add_arrow), FadeOut(add_text),
            FadeOut(sub_arrow), FadeOut(sub_text)
        )
        
        # Calculus symbols: Derivative and Integral
        deriv_sym = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx}", color=COLOR_CALC, font_size=60)
        integ_sym = MathTex(r"\int", color=COLOR_CALC, font_size=72)
        
        self.place_at_grid(deriv_sym, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(integ_sym, "C5")
        
        # Question mark in between to symbolize the search for the link
        question_mark = Text("?", color=WHITE, font_size=72)
        self.place_in_area(question_mark, "C3", "C4")
        
        # Connecting Double Arrow
        connect_arrow = DoubleArrow(
            start=self.grid["C2"] + RIGHT * 0.7,
            end=self.grid["C5"] + LEFT * 0.7,
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=2
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(deriv_sym),
            FadeIn(integ_sym)
        )
        self.play(
            Create(connect_arrow),
            Write(question_mark)
        )
        self.wait(2)

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: The Integral as 'Accumulation'
lecture_lines: Integrals represent the accumulation of values over time.
We calculate this as the area under a curve.
This area sums up all the small changes.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Prerequisite Review: The Integral as 'Accumulation'"
        lines = [
            "Integrals represent the accumulation of values over time.",
            "We calculate this as the area under a curve.",
            "This area sums up all the small changes."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors from storyboard
        COLOR_WHITE = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_BLUE = "#0000FF"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Integrals represent the accumulation of values over time."
        # Visual: Draw a white curve (#FFFFFF) on a black background.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_WHITE))
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE}
        )
        # B035: Padding for axes and scale_factor for area placement
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.85)
        
        # Smooth curve representing a changing value (velocity)
        curve = axes.plot(
            lambda x: 0.1 * x**2 + 0.5 * np.sin(2 * x) + 1.2, 
            x_range=[0, 4.5], 
            color=COLOR_WHITE
        )
        
        # B022/B066/B079: Labels at grid positions matching orientation using raw LaTeX strings
        # x-axis label at bottom right (F6)
        x_label = MathTex(r"t", color=WHITE)
        # y-axis label at top left (A1)
        y_label = MathTex(r"v(t)", color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(x_label, 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(y_label, 'A1', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            Create(axes), 
            Write(x_label), 
            Write(y_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(Create(curve), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "We calculate this as the area under a curve."
        # Visual: Fill the region below with thin Blue (#0000FF) rectangles.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_BLUE)
        )
        
        # Create thin Riemann rectangles to represent discrete summation
        rects = axes.get_riemann_rectangles(
            curve,
            x_range=[0.5, 4.0],
            dx=0.15,
            color=COLOR_BLUE,
            fill_opacity=0.5,
            stroke_width=0.2
        )
        
        self.play(Create(rects, lag_ratio=0.05), run_time=2.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "This area sums up all the small changes."
        # Visual: Merge rectangles into a solid Blue (#0000FF) area block.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_BLUE)
        )
        
        # Smooth area block representing the definite integral
        area = axes.get_area(
            curve,
            x_range=[0.5, 4.0],
            color=COLOR_BLUE,
            fill_opacity=0.8
        )
        
        # Morphing the rectangles into a solid area to show the limit of the sum
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(rects, area), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

        # Reset lecture colors to default for final shot
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

outline.title: Prerequisite Review: The Derivative as a 'Rate'
outline.content: Briefly revisit the derivative as the instantaneous rate of change or the slope of a tangent line. Use a graphical representation of a curve where a moving point shows the changing slope.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: The Derivative as a 'Rate'
lecture_lines: Derivatives measure the instantaneous rate of change.
We visualize this as the slope of a curve.
It tells us how fast a value is changing.
animations: Draw a white curve (#FFFFFF) with a moving point.
Display a yellow tangent line (#FFFF00) at the moving point.
Show the slope value changing as the point moves using the speedometer [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg] to represent the rate of change.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching storyboard data
        title = "Prerequisite Review: The Derivative as a 'Rate'"
        lines = [
            "Derivatives measure the instantaneous rate of change.",
            "We visualize this as the slope of a curve.",
            "It tells us how fast a value is changing."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Define colors for synchronization
        CURVE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        TANGENT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        SLOPE_COLOR = "#00FFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line 1: Derivatives measure the instantaneous rate of change.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(CURVE_COLOR))
        
        # Area B2 to E5 for axes and curve
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": GREY},
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        # Curve: f(x) = 0.5x^2 + 1
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2 + 1, color=CURVE_COLOR)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line 2: We visualize this as the slope of a curve.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(TANGENT_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Tracker for x-coordinate to drive the point and tangent line
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(-1.2)
        
        # Tangent line updated in place
        tangent = Line(color=TANGENT_COLOR)
        def update_tangent(line):
            x0 = x_tracker.get_value()
            y0 = 0.5 * x0**2 + 1
            slope = x0 # Derivative of 0.5x^2 + 1 is x
            # Extend line segments symmetrically from the point
            p1 = axes.c2p(x0 - 0.9, y0 - 0.9 * slope)
            p2 = axes.c2p(x0 + 0.9, y0 + 0.9 * slope)
            line.set_points_as_corners([p1, p2])
        
        # Initial position
        update_tangent(tangent)
        tangent.add_updater(update_tangent)
        
        # Moving point on curve
        dot = Dot(color=TANGENT_COLOR)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 0.5 * x_tracker.get_value()**2 + 1)))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Create(tangent))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line 3: It tells us how fast a value is changing.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(SLOPE_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Slope value label placed at the top of the visualization area
        slope_label = MathTex(r"\text{Slope} = ", color=SLOPE_COLOR)
        slope_value = DecimalNumber(x_tracker.get_value(), num_decimal_places=2, color=SLOPE_COLOR)
        slope_group = VGroup(slope_label, slope_value).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        # Use place_in_area for centering the multi-element group
        self.place_in_area(slope_group, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Efficiently update decimal number value in place
        slope_value.add_updater(lambda v: v.set_value(x_tracker.get_value()))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(slope_group))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Animate the movement of the point, updating tangent and slope display
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(1.2), run_time=5, rate_func=smooth)
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(-1.2), run_time=3, rate_func=smooth)
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: Real-World Application: The Racing Cheetah
outline.content: Apply the concept to physics. If we know the velocity (derivative of position), we can find the total distance (integral). Conversely, if we have the distance, we can find the velocity.
outline.example: A Cheetah sprints. Graph 1 (Velocity): The area under the curve shows the Cheetah moved 100 meters. Graph 2 (Position): The slope of this line at 3 seconds matches the height of Graph 1 at 3 seconds.

outline.title: Summary and Conclusion
outline.content: Recap the 'Inverse' relationship. Emphasize that the integral allows us to find the 'net change' by knowing the 'rate of change', and vice versa.
outline.example: Final split-screen: Left side shows 'Slope Calculation' (Derivative), right side shows 'Area Calculation' (Integral), with a bridge connecting them labeled 'Calculus'.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Teaching Content
        lecture_lines = [
            "- A cheetah's velocity is the derivative of its position.",
            "- The area under the velocity curve is distance traveled.",
            "- We can calculate distance by integrating the velocity function.",
            "- Conversely, differentiate position to find the cheetah's speed.",
            "- These two measurements are mathematically linked."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: The Racing Cheetah", lecture_lines)

        # Color Palette
        VELOCITY_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        AREA_COLOR = "#0000FF"
        POSITION_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        TANGENT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"

        # Velocity Axes and Graph (Top Half)
        ax_v = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 3, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 20},
            tips=False
        )
        labels_v = ax_v.get_axis_labels(x_label="t", y_label="v(t)")
        v_func = lambda t: 0.5 * t
        v_graph = ax_v.plot(v_func, color=VELOCITY_COLOR)
        v_group = VGroup(ax_v, labels_v, v_graph)
        self.place_in_area(v_group, "A1", "C5", scale_factor=0.7)

        # Position Axes and Graph (Bottom Half)
        ax_s = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 20},
            tips=False
        )
        labels_s = ax_s.get_axis_labels(x_label="t", y_label="s(t)")
        s_func = lambda t: 0.25 * t**2
        s_graph = ax_s.plot(s_func, color=POSITION_COLOR)
        s_group = VGroup(ax_s, labels_s, s_graph)
        self.place_in_area(s_group, "D1", "F5", scale_factor=0.7)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(VELOCITY_COLOR))
        self.play(Create(ax_v), Write(labels_v))
        self.play(Create(v_graph))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(AREA_COLOR))
        area = ax_v.get_area(v_graph, x_range=[0, 4], color=AREA_COLOR, opacity=0.4)
        self.play(FadeIn(area))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(AREA_COLOR))
        dist_label = MathTex(r"\text{Dist} = \int_0^4 v(t) dt = 4", color=AREA_COLOR, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(dist_label, "C6", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(dist_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(POSITION_COLOR))
        self.play(Create(ax_s), Write(labels_s))
        self.play(Create(s_graph))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(TANGENT_COLOR))
        
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(2.0)
        
        # Optimized Tangent Line
        tangent_line = Line(color=TANGENT_COLOR)
        def update_tangent(line):
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            m = 0.5 * t # s'(t)
            L = 1.0
            dx = L / np.sqrt(1 + m**2)
            x1, x2 = t - dx, t + dx
            y1, y2 = s_func(t) + m*(x1 - t), s_func(t) + m*(x2 - t)
            line.set_points_as_corners([ax_s.c2p(x1, y1), ax_s.c2p(x2, y2)])
        
        tangent_line.add_updater(update_tangent)
        
        # Synchronized Dots
        dot_v = Dot(color=TANGENT_COLOR)
        dot_v.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(ax_v.c2p(t_tracker.get_value(), v_func(t_tracker.get_value()))))
        
        dot_s = Dot(color=TANGENT_COLOR)
        dot_s.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(ax_s.c2p(t_tracker.get_value(), s_func(t_tracker.get_value()))))
        
        # slope = height labels
        slope_val = DecimalNumber(num_decimal_places=2, color=TANGENT_COLOR, font_size=24)
        slope_val.add_updater(lambda d: d.set_value(0.5 * t_tracker.get_value()))
        slope_label = MathTex(r"\text{Slope} = ", color=TANGENT_COLOR, font_size=24)
        slope_group = VGroup(slope_label, slope_val).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_group, "D6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        height_val = DecimalNumber(num_decimal_places=2, color=TANGENT_COLOR, font_size=24)
        height_val.add_updater(lambda d: d.set_value(0.5 * t_tracker.get_value()))
        height_label = MathTex(r"\text{Height} = ", color=TANGENT_COLOR, font_size=24)
        height_group = VGroup(height_label, height_val).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(height_group, "A6", scale_factor=0.9)

        self.play(Create(tangent_line), Create(dot_v), Create(dot_s))
        self.play(Write(slope_group), Write(height_group))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Interactive movement
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(4.0), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Summary and Conclusion"
        lines = [
            "The Bridge connects rates of change with accumulation.",
            "Derivatives and integrals are two sides of one coin.",
            "This relationship is the heart of calculus."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Define colors
        COLOR_SLOPE = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_AREA = "#0000FF"
        COLOR_BRIDGE = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_TEXT = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Create 'Slope' icon (Rate of Change)
        slope_icon = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=GREY_E), # Axis
            Line(ORIGIN, UP+RIGHT, color=COLOR_SLOPE, stroke_width=8) # Tangent
        )
        slope_label = Text("Slope", font_size=20, color=COLOR_SLOPE)
        slope_group = VGroup(slope_icon, slope_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_group, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Create 'Area' icon (Accumulation)
        area_icon = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=GREY_E), # Axis
            Polygon(ORIGIN, RIGHT*1.5, RIGHT*1.5 + UP, UP*0.5, color=COLOR_AREA, fill_opacity=0.5) # Integral area
        )
        area_label = Text("Area", font_size=20, color=COLOR_AREA)
        area_group = VGroup(area_icon, area_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(area_group, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(slope_group), FadeIn(area_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Draw a gold bridge connecting both icons
        # Coordinates for B2 and B5 centers
        start_point = self.grid["B2"] + RIGHT * 0.5
        end_point = self.grid["B5"] + LEFT * 0.5
        
        bridge_arc = ArcBetweenPoints(start_point, end_point, angle=-TAU/8, color=COLOR_BRIDGE, stroke_width=6)
        bridge_text = Text("Calculus", font_size=24, color=COLOR_BRIDGE)
        
        # Manual placement relative to arc to keep it tidy, but using grid reference as base
        bridge_text.move_to((start_point + end_point)/2 + UP * 0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(bridge_arc), Write(bridge_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Pulse 'Fundamental Theorem of Calculus' text
        ftc_text = Text("Fundamental Theorem\nof Calculus", font_size=32, color=COLOR_TEXT)
        self.place_in_area(ftc_text, "D2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(ftc_text))
        self.play(ftc_text.animate.scale(1.1), run_time=0.5, rate_func=there_and_back)
        self.play(ftc_text.animate.scale(1.1), run_time=0.5, rate_func=there_and_back)
        
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final state
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: Visualizing the Connection: The Area Function
outline.content: Animate a moving vertical line (x) that 'paints' the area under a curve f(t). Show that the rate at which this area grows at any moment is exactly equal to the height of the function at that point.
outline.example: A 'Growing Carpet' animation: As a character unrolls a carpet (the area), the speed at which the carpet area increases is determined by the width of the roll (the function's value f(x)).

storyboard.title: Visualizing the Connection: The Area Function
lecture_lines: Let's define a function for the accumulating area.
As we move right, the total area grows.
The rate of growth depends on the function's height.
Taller curves add area faster than shorter ones.
The derivative of area is the original function.
animations: Draw white curve f(t) and a sliding vertical line.
Shade area behind the sliding line in Yellow (#FFFF00).
Place a red dot (#FF0000) on curve at sliding line.
Show the area's rate of change equals the height f(x).
Flash the connection between area growth and curve height.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Using simple Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX compilation issues (B008)
        title = "Visualizing the Connection: The Area Function"
        lines = [
            "Let's define a function for the accumulating area.",
            "As we move right, the total area grows.",
            "The rate of growth depends on the function's height.",
            "Taller curves add area faster than shorter ones.",
            "The derivative of area is the original function."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_CURVE = WHITE
        COLOR_AREA = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_DOT = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_TEXT = "#00FFFF"

        # Axes setup
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 6, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY},
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Curve f(t) = 0.1t^2 + 1
        func = lambda t: 0.1 * t**2 + 1
        curve = axes.plot(func, x_range=[0, 5.5], color=COLOR_CURVE)
        
        # Use Text instead of MathTex (B008)
        curve_label = Text("f(t)", font_size=20, color=COLOR_CURVE)
        self.place_at_grid(curve_label, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # ValueTracker for x
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Let's define a function for the accumulating area.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_CURVE)
        
        # Sliding vertical line
        # Use a lambda for simple objects but avoid heavy ones
        vline = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_vertical_line(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=2
        ))
        
        # Pre-create text to avoid recreation in always_redraw
        x_label = Text("x", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        x_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(vline, DOWN, buff=0.1))

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), Write(curve_label))
        self.play(Create(vline), FadeIn(x_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # As we move right, the total area grows.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_AREA)
        
        area = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_area(
            curve,
            x_range=[0, x_tracker.get_value()],
            color=COLOR_AREA,
            opacity=0.4
        ))
        
        area_label = Text("A(x) = Area from 0 to x", font_size=20, color=COLOR_AREA)
        self.place_at_grid(area_label, "A3", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.add(area)
        self.play(Write(area_label))
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(4.5), run_time=3, rate_func=rate_functions.linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The rate of growth depends on the function's height.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_DOT)
        
        # Use simple shapes and updates
        dot = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color=COLOR_DOT
        ))
        
        height_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 0),
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color=COLOR_DOT,
            stroke_width=4
        ))
        
        height_label = Text("f(x)", font_size=20, color=COLOR_DOT)
        height_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(dot, UP, buff=0.1))

        self.play(Create(dot), Create(height_line), FadeIn(height_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Taller curves add area faster than shorter ones.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_TEXT)
        
        # Demonstrate growth by moving x again
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=2)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(5.0), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The derivative of area is the original function.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # A'(x) = f(x)
        ftc_formula = Text("Rate of Area Growth = f(x)", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(ftc_formula, "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(ftc_formula))
        self.play(
            Indicate(ftc_formula, color=COLOR_DOT),
            Indicate(height_line, color=COLOR_DOT),
            Indicate(height_label, color=COLOR_DOT),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Bridge: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus",
            [
                "Differentiation and integration are actually inverse processes.",
                "This link is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.",
                "Integrating then differentiating returns the original function.",
                "It connects slopes and areas through a single bridge.",
                "Calculus is a two-way street between these concepts."
            ]
        )

        # Colors
        BLUE_COLOR = "#0000FF"
        GREEN_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the integral expression in Blue (#0000FF).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE_COLOR)
        integral_expr = MathTex(r"\int_{a}^{x} f(t) \, dt", color=BLUE_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(integral_expr, "B2", "C5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(integral_expr))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Surround the integral with a Green (#00FF00) derivative operator.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN_COLOR)
        
        # Create full expression to replace current one
        derivative_op = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx}", r"\left[", r"\int_{a}^{x} f(t) \, dt", r"\right]", color=GREEN_COLOR)
        derivative_op[2].set_color(BLUE_COLOR) # Keep integral blue
        self.place_in_area(derivative_op, "B2", "C5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Transform(integral_expr, derivative_op))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show the expression simplify into the original function f(x).
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE_COLOR)
        
        # Position it to the right of the derivative expression or replace it
        final_eq = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx} \left[ \int_{a}^{x} f(t) \, dt \right] = f(x)")
        # Apply colors to parts
        final_eq[0][:4].set_color(GREEN_COLOR) # d/dx
        final_eq[0][4].set_color(GREEN_COLOR) # [
        final_eq[0][5:13].set_color(BLUE_COLOR) # integral
        final_eq[0][13].set_color(GREEN_COLOR) # ]
        final_eq[0][14:].set_color(WHITE_COLOR) # = f(x)
        
        self.place_in_area(final_eq, "B1", "C6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Transform(integral_expr, final_eq))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Animate a 'Factory' box transforming area back into height.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a simple factory box
        factory_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=1.5, color=GREY, fill_opacity=0.5)
        factory_label = Text("FTC Factory", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        factory_group = VGroup(factory_box, factory_label)
        self.place_in_area(factory_group, "E2", "F5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Area representation (Input)
        area_rect = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=0.5, color=BLUE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8)
        area_label = Text("Area", font_size=14, color=BLUE_COLOR)
        area_in = VGroup(area_rect, area_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(area_in, "E1")
        
        # Height representation (Output)
        height_line = Line(ORIGIN, UP * 0.8, color=WHITE_COLOR, stroke_width=4)
        height_label = Text("f(x)", font_size=14, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        height_out = VGroup(height_line, height_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(height_out, "E6")

        self.play(Create(factory_group))
        self.play(FadeIn(area_in))
        
        # Move Area into factory, then output f(x)
        self.play(area_in.animate.move_to(factory_group.get_center()))
        self.play(FadeOut(area_in))
        self.play(FadeIn(height_out, shift=RIGHT))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Highlight the final f(x) in White (#FFFFFF) with a glow.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE_COLOR)
        
        # Create a "glow" effect using multiple rectangles
        glows = VGroup(*[
            SurroundingRectangle(integral_expr, color=WHITE, buff=0.1 + i*0.05, stroke_width=2)
            for i in range(3)
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(glows))
        self.play(
            glows.animate.set_stroke(width=10, opacity=0.3),
            run_time=1,
            rate_func=there_and_back
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Using simple Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX compilation issues (B008)
        title = "Visualizing the Connection: The Area Function"
        lines = [
            "Let's define a function for the accumulating area.",
            "As we move right, the total area grows.",
            "The rate of growth depends on the function's height.",
            "Taller curves add area faster than shorter ones.",
            "The derivative of area is the original function."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_CURVE = WHITE
        COLOR_AREA = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_DOT = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_TEXT = "#00FFFF"

        # Axes setup
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 6, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY},
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4
        )
        # Fix for Issue #41: Adjusted area to prevent overlap with ftc_formula
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B1', 'E6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Curve f(t) = 0.1t^2 + 1
        func = lambda t: 0.1 * t**2 + 1
        curve = axes.plot(func, x_range=[0, 5.5], color=COLOR_CURVE)
        
        # Use Text instead of MathTex (B008)
        curve_label = Text("f(t)", font_size=20, color=COLOR_CURVE)
        self.place_at_grid(curve_label, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # ValueTracker for x
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Let's define a function for the accumulating area.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_CURVE)
        
        # Sliding vertical line
        vline = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_vertical_line(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=2
        ))
        
        # Pre-create text to avoid recreation in always_redraw
        x_label = Text("x", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        x_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(vline, DOWN, buff=0.1))

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), Write(curve_label))
        self.play(Create(vline), FadeIn(x_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # As we move right, the total area grows.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_AREA)
        
        area = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_area(
            curve,
            x_range=[0, x_tracker.get_value()],
            color=COLOR_AREA,
            opacity=0.4
        ))
        
        area_label = Text("A(x) = Area from 0 to x", font_size=20, color=COLOR_AREA)
        # Fix for Issue #42: Better centering for long label
        self.place_in_area(area_label, 'A2', 'A5', scale_factor=0.8)

        self.add(area)
        self.play(Write(area_label))
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(4.5), run_time=3, rate_func=rate_functions.linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The rate of growth depends on the function's height.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_DOT)
        
        # Use simple shapes and updates
        dot = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color=COLOR_DOT
        ))
        
        height_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 0),
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color=COLOR_DOT,
            stroke_width=4
        ))
        
        height_label = Text("f(x)", font_size=20, color=COLOR_DOT)
        height_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(dot, UP, buff=0.1))

        self.play(Create(dot), Create(height_line), FadeIn(height_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Taller curves add area faster than shorter ones.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_TEXT)
        
        # Demonstrate growth by moving x again
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=2)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(5.0), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The derivative of area is the original function.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Rate of Area Growth = f(x)
        ftc_formula = Text("Rate of Area Growth = f(x)", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        # Fix for Issue #43: Centered long label at bottom
        self.place_in_area(ftc_formula, 'F2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(ftc_formula))
        self.play(
            Indicate(ftc_formula, color=COLOR_DOT),
            Indicate(height_line, color=COLOR_DOT),
            Indicate(height_label, color=COLOR_DOT),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

            "It tells us how fast a value is changing."

        # Define colors for synchronization
        CURVE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        TANGENT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"

            line.set_points_as_corners([p1, p2])

        # Asset: speedometer.svg
        speedometer_asset = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg"
        speedometer = SVGMobject(speedometer_asset, color=SLOPE_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(speedometer, "A5", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Needle for speedometer
        needle = Line(ORIGIN, UP * 0.3, color=RED, stroke_width=4)

            val = x_tracker.get_value() # slope range is approx -1.2 to 1.2
            # Map slope to angle. Let 0 be UP (PI/2).

            angle = -val * (PI/3)

            # The speedometer SVG center is used as the pivot.
            n.set_points_as_corners([

                center + 0.35 * np.array([np.cos(PI/2 + angle), np.sin(PI/2 + angle), 0])
            ])

        needle.add_updater(update_needle)
        
        # Efficiently update decimal number value in place
        slope_value.add_updater(lambda v: v.set_value(x_tracker.get_value()))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(slope_group), FadeIn(speedometer), Create(needle))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Animate the movement of the point, updating tangent and slope display
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(1.2), run_time=5, rate_func=rate_functions.smooth)
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(-1.2), run_time=3, rate_func=rate_functions.smooth)
        self.wait(2)
